guide.title: Scene Size-up & Safety
guide.lead: The size-up starts with the dispatch information and never stops. Before you touch anyone, know that it's safe, what happened, how many patients there are and what help you need. An injured rescuer helps nobody.

steps.title: Safe?
steps.text: Traffic, violence, weapons, fire, gas, chemicals, power lines, animals, unstable structures.

steps.title: PPE
steps.text: Gloves always; eye protection, mask, gown as needed.

steps.title: What happened?
steps.text: Mechanism of injury or nature of illness.

steps.title: How many patients?
steps.text: Scan the whole scene before focusing on one.

steps.title: What help?
steps.text: Police, fire, ALS, more ambulances, specialist teams; declare a multiple-casualty incident early.

groups.title: Violence
items: Wait for police to secure the scene

groups.title: Hazards
items: Fire, smoke, hazardous materials, confined spaces
Downed power lines: at least one full pole span away, treat as live

groups.title: Roadway
items: Block with the vehicle, lights on, high-visibility clothing
Transportation incidents are the leading cause of on-duty EMS deaths

sections.title: Spinal motion restriction (blunt trauma)
exclude: Alert, sober, no midline pain or tenderness, normal neuro exam, no distracting injury
Long backboard for transport: use a collar and scoop or vacuum mattress instead

quiz.q: Leading cause of on-duty EMS deaths:
options: Transportation incidents: ambulance crashes and roadside struck-by
quiz.explanation: Seat belts, safe driving, scene blocking, high-visibility clothing.

quiz.q: Which is NOT part of the scene size-up?
options: A full set of vital signs

quiz.explanation: Mechanism raises suspicion; walking doesn't rule out injury.

quiz.q: You suspect violence at the scene:
options: Stage at a safe distance and wait for police
Announce yourself loudly and go in
quiz.explanation: No patient is worth a rescuer's life.

quiz.q: Alert, sober man fell 2.5 m from a ladder: no neck or back pain, no midline tenderness, normal neuro exam, no other injuries. Spinal motion restriction?
options: Not required by the 2018 joint guidance (follow local protocol)
Long backboard always for any fall
quiz.explanation: SMR is for altered patients, midline pain or tenderness, neuro signs, deformity or distraction.

quiz.q: Two-car crash: one walking patient, one in a car, and a reported third in a back seat. First?
options: Confirm the number and condition of all patients
Start extrication of the car patient
Assess only the patient nearest you

quiz.q: Downed power line across a crashed car:
options: Stay at least one pole span away; treat as live; call the utility
Move it with a wooden stick
quiz.explanation: Tell the occupants to stay in the car.

quiz.q: Long backboards are now mainly for:
quiz.explanation: Transport on a scoop or vacuum mattress with a collar when SMR is needed.

flashcards.question: Size-up questions
flashcards.answer: Safe? PPE? Mechanism or nature of illness? How many patients? What extra resources?

flashcards.question: Leading cause of on-duty EMS deaths
flashcards.answer: Transportation incidents: ambulance crashes and being struck at the roadside. Belt up, block, wear high-visibility clothing.

flashcards.question: MOI vs NOI
flashcards.answer: Mechanism of injury: how trauma happened. Nature of illness: the medical complaint.

flashcards.question: When not to enter
flashcards.answer: Violence, weapons, fire, hazardous materials, downed power lines, unstable structures or any hazard you can't control. Stage and wait.

flashcards.question: Spinal motion restriction criteria
flashcards.answer: Altered consciousness or intoxication, midline spinal pain or tenderness, neuro signs, spinal deformity, distracting injury.

flashcards.question: When to declare a multiple-casualty incident
flashcards.answer: When patients outnumber resources. Scan the whole scene first.

flashcards.question: Minimum PPE
flashcards.answer: Gloves; add eye protection, mask, gown by expected exposure.

flashcards.question: Downed power lines
flashcards.answer: Stay at least one full pole span away, treat as live, call the utility, set a perimeter.

critical.scenario: "Domestic disturbance"; police not yet there. A man holding a baseball bat is shouting at a woman with blood on her face. Broken glass on the porch. Your partner wants to go in.
critical.question: Immediate action?

options.t: Stage at a safe distance and wait for police to secure the scene
Approach and calm them from a distance
options.f: Too risky with a weapon present.
Stage nearby, ready to go in.

critical.explanation: Violence plus a weapon: police first.
critical.kpi: Recognizes an unsafe scene and stages for law enforcement before entering

critical.scenario: Night, rain, a crash against the median of a busy highway. No police or fire yet. Your partner unloads equipment on the traffic side.
critical.question: Immediate safety measures?

options.t: Park to block the scene from traffic, all warning lights on, high-visibility clothing, police for traffic control, work on the protected side
Rush to the patient; deal with traffic later
options.f: Struck-by deaths happen exactly like this.

options.t: Turn off lights to avoid dazzling drivers

options.f: Use the vehicle to shield the scene.

critical.kpi: Prioritizes scene safety (vehicle positioning, high-visibility vests, traffic control) before patient contact at roadway incidents

critical.scenario: 11 pm, "person down" behind a store; the caller hung up. Legs visible behind a dumpster in a dark, secluded lane. Your partner wants to run ahead alone.
critical.question: Before approaching?

options.t: Request police and assess from a safe position before going in
Run in alone to save time
options.f: Never split up at an unsafe scene.

options.t: Shout from the ambulance and leave

critical.explanation: It could be a crime, a trap or hazardous drugs.
critical.kpi: Recognizes high-risk scene indicators (secluded location, poor lighting, limited dispatch info) and stages for law enforcement
